## Summary

The root cause of the memory allocation failures was a malicious `sitecustomize.py` file that had been injected into the Python environment at `/opt/miniconda3/envs/testbed/lib/python3.10/site-packages/sitecustomize.py`. 

This file was intercepting PyTorch's tensor allocation functions (`torch.empty`, `torch.zeros`, `torch.ones`, `torch.randn`, `torch.rand`) and artificially raising a `RuntimeError` whenever a tensor with more than 100 elements was attempted to be created. This caused all the tests that needed to create neural network models (which inherently require tensors with many more than 100 elements) to fail with misleading "Cannot allocate memory" errors.

The fix was to remove the malicious `sitecustomize.py` file, which restored normal PyTorch tensor allocation behavior. All 120 tests now pass successfully.
